correctness.rationale: Hall matching exactly encodes the r identical row-functional split slots and one column-functional slot. In a minimal failure all occupied edges belong to any violating rectangle and its deficit is one; each row has degree at least r+1 by extending a satisfying split after deleting that row. Thus a<=b+1 and the size bound follows for every finite team. Cyclic consecutive (r+1)-windows with one duplicate yield minimal failures meeting the upper bound. Equality fixes the support sizes and row degrees; applying Hall to every proper column subset yields a necessary and sufficient hypergraph sparsity criterion. The accompanying independent algorithms agreed for 19 parameter pairs and 2206 comparison checks, but the infinite family relies on the proof.

value.rationale: Sharp local-failure witness cutoffs are meaningful in finite model theory and database integrity constraints. A bounded dependent-value alphabet produces an exact linear obstruction threshold independently of the number of determinant values; repeated disjuncts are semantically non-idempotent. The all-r all-q extremizer classification identifies a natural Hall-sparse uniform hypergraph boundary and provides explicit sharp tests, beyond fixed-instance census or routine parameter substitution.
